title: Threads: creating, starting and what one really costs

videos.script: The second half of this course is about doing several things at once, and it starts with the oldest tool Java has for it: the thread. {{start}} A thread runs a Runnable, and it starts when you call start. Call run instead and nothing new happens: the same thread does the work, and the program is not concurrent at all. {{states}} A thread lives through a few states, new, runnable, waiting and terminated, and you can watch it move between them. {{cost}} Then the price. A thousand threads start in a fraction of a second and take tens of megabytes. Ten thousand take seconds. Every one of them is a thread of the operating system. {{die}} And last, what happens when a thread throws an exception nobody catches. It dies, it prints a stack trace, and the rest of the program carries on as if nothing happened.
